name: Clock
description: A native clock — alarms and timers your agent sets for itself, and you set in the GUI.
about: Clatch has no cron; a scheduler is just an app that fires signals. Clock is that app, built like a real clock: a live analog face, drum-wheel alarms, and a countdown timer. The agent schedules its own alarms and timers over the CLI, the human sets them in the GUI, and when one is due it fires a run-type signal that wakes the agent(s) the alarm targets — chosen in the GUI (or with --to), defaulting to whoever set it.

commands.name: list
commands.about: list all alarms and timers (shows who each wakes)

commands.name: alarm
commands.about: set an alarm at a wall-clock time; --note is your prompt for the turn it wakes, --repeat daily|weekdays|weekends|mon,wed,fri, --to picks which agent(s) it wakes, --quiet fires as context without a turn

commands.name: edit
commands.about: change an alarm; omitted flags keep their value (--time --label --note --repeat --quiet --wake --to)

commands.name: timer
commands.about: start a countdown (10m, 1h30m, 90s) — fires timer.done when it ends

commands.name: set
commands.about: shorthand: a clock time makes an alarm, a duration a timer

commands.name: hide
commands.about: send it back to the background — the alarms keep running

commands.name: close
commands.about: quit the app — this is what stops the alarms
